idea: labeler comparison with G-Eval-style rubric guidance (g1: rich criteria + per-level anchors, soft labels)
change: deepseek-v4.1-flash / claude-haiku-5.5 / gemini-2.5-flash-lite / qwen3.7-flash, all with g1
takeaway: qwen3.7-flash is both the cheapest and the best labeler on dev (0.557)

idea: rubric guidance vs plain task prompt (qwen)
change: plain spec questions vs g1 rubric
takeaway: the rubric (definitions, per-level anchors, 'ignore tokenisation artefacts') is worth +0.13 dev

idea: 20 gold seeds as few-shot examples in the labeling prompt
takeaway: seeds hurt qwen (-0.08), helped deepseek a bit; seeds share docs with dev so even this is optimistic

idea: CoT: short 'analysis' field before the scores (qwen)
takeaway: alone worse than greedy g1, but useful as an extra vote in a self-consistency ensemble

idea: self-consistency: average soft labels of several qwen samples (T=0.7) + greedy
change: x3 = greedy+2 samples; x5 = greedy+3 samples+CoT
takeaway: teacher improves +0.02-0.04 with votes; applied to the 1376 pool texts

idea: cross-model label ensembles (qwen x3 + haiku / deepseek / gemini)
takeaway: +haiku +0.014 (noise level), not worth $0.5 on the pool

idea: CPU latency probe of gte-modernbert int8 ONNX vs layers and sequence length (stock HF export, sdpa)
takeaway: full inputs (~560-790 tokens) are 10-20x over the gate; stock export spends most time in Where/IsNaN mask ops

idea: eager attention export instead of sdpa
takeaway: removes the O(L^2) mask ops; budget is ~16 layers x 192 tokens or 22 x 128

idea: export-friendly ModernBERT forward (precomputed rotary tables, rotate_half as constant matmul, one window mask)
takeaway: ~10-20% faster and more stable p95 under load

idea: layer-truncated gte-modernbert x input length (shared encoder, 4 heads, lexical features, soft labels, qwen g1 labels)
takeaway: long article context does not help the student; 16 layers x 192 tokens fits the gate and is best

idea: more epochs (8 vs 4-6)
takeaway: dev peaks at epoch 5-6; 6 epochs fixed

idea: within-article pairwise ranking loss on expected scores
takeaway: no gain over soft-label KL

idea: drop the lexical alignment features (full-article n-gram novelty, lead coverage, repetition, truncation)
takeaway: features are within noise but kept (cheap, give the model full-article signal)

idea: lr 5e-5 vs 3e-5
takeaway: no gain

idea: train the student on self-consistency labels (x3) instead of greedy x1
takeaway: better teacher (+0.02 on dev) transfers only marginally to the student

idea: aligned context: summary + article sentences chosen by lexical overlap with the summary (+ lead sentence) instead of the article lead
takeaway: small consistent gain on consistency/relevance; kept

idea: LLM-generated summaries with controlled quality profiles (18 profiles: hallucination, disfluent, incoherent order, redundant, truncated, off-focus, extractive variants...), 9 per article call, PTB/lowercase style mimicry, labeled by qwen g1
takeaway: synthetic flaws are much grosser than the real system-vs-system differences; student shifts to novelty cues and loses within-article ranking

idea: synthetic variants: weight 0.3 / exclude consistency head / drop hallucination profiles
takeaway: every mix of LLM-written synthetic summaries is below real-only

idea: programmatic extractive summaries in SummEval-system style (lead-3, lead-2, random/late sentences, duplicated sentence, length-capped lead), LLM-labeled
change: +560 synthetic to real (align ctx, x3 labels)
takeaway: even in-distribution-looking synthetic summaries hurt

idea: LLM-written CNN/DM-style new articles (281) as a source for synthetic summaries
takeaway: not used: synthetic summaries failed on real articles first

idea: add dev gold (one half of dev docs) to training, evaluate on the other half
takeaway: mixing 110 gold (sharp, mostly-4 targets) into LLM soft labels hurts; gold not used for training

idea: add LLM (x3) labels of dev-half texts (more real-distribution data), evaluate on the other half
takeaway: +100 real texts is neutral: data volume is not the bottleneck

idea: student-teacher fidelity on held-out fold 0 (group Spearman student vs qwen x3 labels)
takeaway: the 16L/192 student reproduces only ~0.6-0.7 of the teacher's within-article ranking

idea: weight soup of 3 seeds
takeaway: seeds land in different basins (different head init); prediction ensembles help (+0.02) but cost latency

idea: x5 labels (greedy + 3 samples + CoT) for the student
takeaway: teacher x5 is better on dev but the student does not gain

idea: pool CLS + masked mean instead of CLS
takeaway: +0.01 and lower seed variance; kept

idea: dynamic int8 (per-channel) of every weight MatMul of the 16L student
takeaway: full int8 costs ~0.03 dev mean consistently across the 5 fold models

idea: keep selected MatMuls in fp32 (fold-0 model): rotary R / attention out / MLP down-projection
takeaway: the GLU down-projection (outlier activations) is the int8-sensitive op; fp32 there recovers fp32 accuracy for ~6% latency (A/B interleaved, loaded machine)

idea: frozen round-1 recipe: 16L gte-modernbert, 192 tokens (summary + overlap-selected article sentences), CLS+mean pooling, 17 lexical full-article features, 4 heads, soft-label KL on qwen3.7-flash x5 self-consistency labels, 6 epochs, 5-fold cross-fit by document, mixed int8 ONNX (MLP down-proj fp32)
takeaway: dev ~0.50 vs teacher 0.60; Jev 0.554 on test, so a win is unlikely but the recipe is the best found on dev

idea: CPU latency of the frozen pipeline (fold-0 model, mixed int8 ONNX, fast ModernBERT export, includes rendering+tokenisation+features)
takeaway: passes the 70 ms gate with ~15 ms margin at moderate load; fails under heavy load (load>10)

idea: LLM sentence-level fact verification: summary split into sentences, qwen3.7-flash judges each vs the article (supported/minor/unsupported/contradicted); score = mean support
takeaway: verification alone matches/exceeds the rubric labeler on consistency (0.59 vs 0.57) but blending it into the teacher's consistency target does not help; used as an auxiliary distillation target instead

idea: sentence verification of all 1376 eval texts (aux target) + 'natural' weak-model summaries pilot: 45 training-fold articles x 3 cheap LLMs (qwen, gemini-2.5-flash-lite, deepseek) x 4 plain prompts, T=1.0, PTB-styled 65%, labeled qwen g1 x3 + verified
takeaway: data generated; student results logged separately

idea: auxiliary head distilling the LLM sentence-verification score (BCE, w=0.5); optional inference mix into consistency
takeaway: the student cannot learn the verification signal from 192 tokens (aux head 0.41 vs LLM 0.59); no gain, not mixed in

idea: natural weak-model summaries pilot (539, 45 articles) for all 4 heads
takeaway: consistency +0.04 on every seed but fluency/relevance drop; mean unchanged

idea: natural weak-model summaries pilot, used only for the consistency head (other heads masked on synthetic rows)
takeaway: +0.015, every seed above every baseline seed

idea: scale natural summaries to all 86 eval articles (+492, 41 more articles; qwen x3 labels), consistency-head only
takeaway: +0.03 dev over round 1 (all seeds); shared encoder improves coherence/fluency too

idea: round-2 frozen recipe: round-1 student + 1031 natural weak-LLM summaries (all 86 eval articles, in-fold) as consistency-head targets
takeaway: beats round 1 on dev beyond noise -> re-scored once on test (round 2). Bookkeeping slip: FROZEN.json's dev_metrics/latency blocks were the stale round-1 files (description has the correct round-2 dev evidence); corrected copies in dev_metrics_round2.json / latency_round2.json

idea: CPU latency of the round-2 pipeline (r2_f0, same architecture)
takeaway: p95 ~56 ms, under the 70 ms gate

idea: all 22 layers of gte-modernbert (no truncation) at 192/256/320 tokens, round-2 data
takeaway: the full-depth model is consistently worse (-0.05 to -0.08) on this tiny, noisy-label set, as in round 1; depth is not the lever

idea: prediction ensemble of 2-3 seeds of the round-2 16x192 student (fold-0 selection runs)
takeaway: +0.01 (2 models) / +0.018 (3 models) on fold-0 selection runs; 2 models fit 8 threads if single-model p95 is ~half the gate

idea: longer inputs with the 16-layer student: 256 and 320 tokens (more overlap-selected article context), round-2 data
takeaway: more article context lowers dev by ~0.02 (all seeds); fluency/relevance drop, consistency mixed

idea: cross-fitted seed ensembles of the round-2 student (5 folds x seeds 0,1,2; int8), paired bootstrap over 14 dev articles vs round-2 frozen recipe
change: average probabilities of 2 or 3 seed models per fold
takeaway: ensembles help by +0.008/+0.012 but the 95% CIs include 0, so the rule for re-scoring is not met; not re-scored

idea: 8-thread CPU latency: round-2 single model vs 2/3-model ensembles (separate ORT sessions)
takeaway: single model has p95 ~38 ms on 8 threads; two 8-thread ORT sessions interfere (thread-pool spinning), so a 2-model ensemble needs both encoders in one graph to hope for ~70 ms; ensemble gain too small to pursue
